societies.name: Outer Wilds: Echoes of the Eye — The Stranger’s simulation residents
societies.work: Outer Wilds: Echoes of the Eye
societies.society: Active alien-derived persons continuing inside their maintained simulation

scope.continuity: Released Echoes of the Eye expansion
scope.period: The established long-running simulation before the observed dam/tower failure
scope.population: Active minds of the Stranger’s former biological inhabitants, an explicit alien-person proxy
exclusions: Dead biological bodies as a second population
Disconnected or extinguished minds as ongoing residents
An independently ruling AI inferred from the environment

societies.description:
The Stranger’s inhabitants establish a shared simulation of their lost home and continue experiencing it after their biological bodies die. The maintained technological environment supplies ongoing residence and recreation without an outside living workforce or current wages. This is an active alien-derived community, explicitly used as a person proxy, rather than a collection of unconscious corpses. Its material guarantee estimate is moderately strong but broad: continued existence depends on physical artifacts and fires, and the later dam failure can extinguish access permanently.

The inhabitants themselves built and operate the system, but the references do not establish how control of its underlying productive substrate is divided. Patrols, secrecy and the imprisonment of a dissenter reveal social coercion without proving either equal ownership or an autonomous AI sovereign. Control therefore remains unresolved and the regime label provisional. Music, guarding, care and other useful activities can still count as work; a recreated homeworld is not a participation census. Biological bodies, inactive files and the temporary visitor do not enlarge the active resident denominator.

guarantees.basis: Long-lasting active virtual life is maintained, but artifact/fire dependence and later flooding can end it.

control.basis: Residents create/use the environment and enforce social restrictions, but effective ownership of its sustaining substrate is not specified.

nonworking.basis: Recreation coexists with useful music, guarding and other possible work; no active-person census is supplied.

evidence.claim: Former biological inhabitants actively persist in an implemented simulation after bodily death, dependent on physical artifacts/fires.
evidence.locator: Simulation connection/after-death and long-duration inhabitant sections

uncertainties: Alien-derived active-person proxy, not human biological residents.
Physical corpses and disconnected minds are excluded.
Machine environment is not assumed to be an AI government.

review.method: Second pass against the gathered passages, including explicit uncertainty; no independent reviewer

societies.name: Warhammer 40,000 — AI-provided Dark Age colonies
societies.society: The human colonies explicitly described as utopias under machine administration

scope.continuity: Dark Age background described in Warhammer 40,000 rulebook lore
scope.period: Established machine-provided colony life before the Cybernetic Revolt
scope.population: Living humans in the described provision colonies
exclusions: All human-settled worlds as identical utopias
Every historical human empire as one political unit

societies.description:
Dark Age lore explicitly describes thinking machines transforming human colonies into utopias by administering to every need. That supplies more than an inference from advanced weapons or Standard Template Constructs: ongoing material provision is part of the stated arrangement. The record is limited to those described colonies, not every human world across a diverse era. Guarantees are rated strong within the functioning order, while the later machine rebellion is excluded as a different period and a warning about its vulnerability.

Effective control remains unresolved. Machines administer provision, but references also describe them as human servants; neither daily management nor the later revolt proves that humans lacked authority beforehand. The provisional AI-provision regime therefore retains a human-control alternative. Freedom from subsistence work does not establish that people stopped research, care or creation, so nonworking stays null. Tabletop background is the verified medium here; unrelated games and every novel set in the franchise are not automatically tagged as depicting this same colony economy.

guarantees.basis: The lore directly describes machine-administered provision of every need in the scoped colonies; no uniform galaxywide guarantee is inferred.

control.basis: Machine administration and human-master language coexist; actual override/property powers are unresolved.

nonworking.basis: Needs provision and freedom from necessary work do not census useful chosen activity.

evidence.claim: Thinking machines provide for every need of the described human colony utopias.
evidence.locator: Artificial Intelligence section, with rulebook citations

uncertainties: Specific described colony type, not all Dark Age humanity.
Pre-rebellion scope; no post-collapse security score.
Machine administration does not settle sovereignty or ownership.
Only the verified tabletop background medium is tagged.

review.method: Second pass against the gathered passages, including explicit uncertainty; no independent reviewer

societies.name: Warhammer 40,000 — Pre-Fall Aeldari construct economy
societies.society: The established automated Aeldari paradise-world order before its final social collapse

scope.continuity: Aeldari pre-Fall lore described through codex and prose references
scope.period: The mature construct-supported empire before the final violent collapse and Fall
scope.population: Living Aeldari residents, an explicit biological alien-person proxy
exclusions: The final possessed/anarchic population as unchanged security
Artificial constructs as additional biological residents

societies.description:
The pre-Fall Aeldari delegate basic economic functions to psychomatons and spirit-drones, enabling residents of their paradise worlds to pursue curiosity, art and leisure. This is explicit productive replacement rather than a conclusion drawn from longevity or psychic power alone. Guarantees are rated strong within the established order, with uncertainty about individual rights and uneven local rule. The final descent into violence and the catastrophe of the Fall are separate conditions, not assigned this earlier material-security score.

The empire has varied rulers and aristocracies rather than a verified single democratic constitution. The control estimate therefore lies near concentrated organic authority, used openly as an alien-person analogy rather than mistaking artificial workers for sovereign AI. A high, low-confidence nonworking estimate follows the substantial release from ordinary economic work and widespread indulgence, with a wide allowance for useful arts, exploration, study and other chosen activity. It is not a canonical census. Later Craftworld discipline and Exodite labor are not automatically the same economy, and constructs are not counted as biological Aeldari residents.

guarantees.basis: Constructs cover basic economic functions and luxuries in the established order; individual entitlements and local exclusions remain incompletely described.

control.basis: Varied organic rulers/aristocracies are the concentrated non-AI reference by explicit analogy; robot labor is not proof of AI government.

nonworking.basis: Broad freedom from ordinary production and extensive indulgence support a directional estimate, while useful chosen arts/research still count.

evidence.claim: Artificial constructs perform basic economic functions while living Aeldari pursue inclinations and leisure.
evidence.locator: Before the Fall and government/overview sections

uncertainties: Established economy before the final violent breakdown.
Broad editorial participation estimate, not a census.
Local political variety and construct ontology remain limitations.

review.method: Second pass against the gathered passages, including explicit uncertainty; no independent reviewer

review_notes: Twelve ordered decisions and three scoped records; no complete game transcript, novel or codex read.
The Stranger’s active alien-derived persons are distinguished from corpses and from an assumed AI sovereign. Fires/hardware can withdraw continued existence.
Dark Age colony utopias are a specified subset, not homogeneous humanity. Pre-Fall Aeldari provision is not imported into later Craftworlds.
A No Man’s Sky player-created monarchy, Warhammer fan campaigns, real-world Craftworld businesses and unrelated fiction were discarded.
Denied wiki access was respected; indexed passages are labeled. Official Necron unit text does not justify claiming every dynasty’s mind or economy is identical.
